Multi-layer attention analysis (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:multilayer_attention}) shows that the trained model maintains substantial instruction attention at all sampled layers (mean text attention $> 46\%$), with elevated attention at both L1 (25/32 heads, $57.7\%$) and L31 (19/32, $56.3\%$).

tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Reorganization of routing across depth.}
The 32-layer attention profile (Figure~\ref{fig:attention_profile}) reveals qualitatively distinct routing patterns.
Llama-2 base concentrates instruction attention at mid-depth: few instruction-dominant heads at L0--L4 (0--10), a peak at L9--L16 (15--22 heads), and a decline at L31 (8 heads), consistent with typical autoregressive LM processing depth.
VLA fine-tuning shifts this to an entry-exit pattern: instruction-dominant heads concentrate at L0--L1 (21--24) and L31 (18), with intermediate layers showing markedly fewer (0--11 at L2--L30).
The untrained model maintains 0 instruction-dominant heads at all 32 layers.
This pattern shift suggests that VLA training reorganizes \emph{when} instruction information is accessed, concentrating it at the network entry and exit rather than at mid-depth.

\paragraph{Synthesis and implications.}
Our experiments reveal a coherent picture: image tokens remain purely visual across all 32 layers, while the readout token is the sole multimodal convergence point.
VLA fine-tuning reorganizes instruction routing from mid-depth (L9--L16) to an entry-exit pattern (L0--L1 and L31), enabling immediate instruction access ($99.6\%$ vs.\ pretrained $80.2\%$); untrained routing never exceeds $10\%$.
Training effects concentrate at the readout token ($R^2$ $+0.069$) rather than image representations ($\Delta \leq 1.7\%$), with the LLM transforming vision encoder geometry non-monotonically (L8--L13 most action-relevant).
Vision encoder pretraining quality is thus the primary design lever; since instructions route solely through the readout token ($|\Delta| < 0.006$; \cite{grant2026}), architectures should optimize routing to this position.

\paragraph{Limitations.}
We study OpenVLA-7B on LIBERO tabletop tasks; generalization to other architectures (e.g., RT-2~\cite{brohan2023_rt2}, $\pi_0$~\cite{black2024_pi0}), locomotion, or dexterous manipulation remains open.
MLP probes may underestimate representational capacity, and our post-hoc analyses do not address whether architectural interventions would preserve action quality in closed-loop evaluation.

1	Vision-language-action models (VLAs) fine-tune large language models (LLMs) on robot demonstrations, but how they internally process multimodal information at the token level remains unknown.
2	We perform a systematic token-level representational decomposition of a VLA (OpenVLA-7B on LIBERO) with factorial trained-vs-untrained control, combining cross-instruction probes, attention analysis, Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA), and functional probes across all 32 LLM layers.
3	Three findings emerge.
4	First, the VLA exhibits strict token-level functional specialization: image tokens encode purely visual information (instruction classification at chance, $10\%$, across all layers), while the readout token serves as a multimodal convergence point ($100\%$ instruction classification from L1, cross-validated).
5	Second, VLA fine-tuning reorganizes instruction routing across depth: language pretraining concentrates instruction attention at mid-depth (L9--L16, 15--22 heads), while VLA training shifts this to an entry-exit pattern (L0--L1: 21--24 heads, L31: 18 heads), enabling immediate instruction access ($99.6\%$ at L1 vs.\ pretrained $80.2\%$); untrained routing never exceeds $10\%$.
6	Third, the LLM applies a non-monotonic refinement of vision encoder geometry: RSA peaks at L12, probe $R^2$ peaks at L8--L13, with self-supervised DINOv2 providing the highest geometric foundation ($\rho = 0.692$, exceeding all internal representations).
7	These results reveal that VLAs maintain a strict division of labor between visual and multimodal tokens, with training primarily reshaping readout-token information integration (routing $+18$pp, attention $+46$pp) rather than visual representations ($\Delta \leq 1.7\%$).
8	These findings suggest that routing efficiency to the readout position may be a key design consideration; vision encoder quality emerges as a candidate lever for action-relevant representation quality.
